papers.summary: Abstract Inspection robots are usually used in challenging and narrow environments like mines, underground pipe galleries and closed industrial workshops. These areas pose practical difficulties, such as poor lighting, small corridors, and crowded barriers, and the absence of existing maps. To accomplish tasks of inspection safely, robots need to have good obstacle avoidance and powerful navigation. papers.summary: Introduction Robotic-assisted therapy (RAT) has emerged as a promising intervention for post-stroke recovery; however, its implementation in developing countries such as Indonesia remains limited by economic, technical, and systemic barriers. papers.title: Reward function compression facilitates goal-dependent reinforcement learning
papers.summary: Abstract Humans can uniquely assign value to novel, abstract outcomes to support reinforcement learning. However, this flexibility is cognitively costly and reduces learning efficiency. We propose that goal-dependent learning initially relies on capacity-limited working memory. With consistent experience, learners create a compressed reward function — a simplified rule — that transfers to long-term memory for automatic evaluation upon receiving feedback. papers.title: Human, AI, and Hybrid Ensembles for Detection of Adaptive, RL-based Social Bots
papers.summary: The use of reinforcement learning to dynamically adapt and evade detection is now well-documented in several cybersecurity settings including Covert Social Influence Operations (CSIOs), in which bots try to spread disinformation. While AI bot detectors have improved greatly, they are largely limited to detecting static bots that do not adapt dynamically. We present the first systematic study comparing the ability of humans, AI models, and hybrid Human-AI ensembles in detecting adaptive bots powered by reinforcement learning (RL) . papers.title: Controller Mimicking for On-the-Fly DES Reachability Control
papers.summary: One of the primary challenges in synthesizing controllers for Discrete Event Systems (DES) is the exponential growth of the composed state space. On-the-fly Directed Controller Synthesis (OTF-DCS) mitigates this by incrementally exploring the system, but its performance depends on the quality of the exploration heuristic. Recent reinforcement learning approaches learn effective heuristics but require repeatedly executing the expensive OTF-DCS algorithm during training, making the process computationally heavy.

papers.title: Antcar: Simple Route Following Task with Ants-Inspired Vision and Neural Model
papers.summary: The goal of this project is to develop a new method of Route following for mobile robots in a GNSSdenied environment like urban canyons or indoor. A visual compass algorithm consists in determining the orientation of the maximum familiarity index with respect to the learned panoramas along a path. papers.title: DermArtifactDB: a multi-label dataset for artifact annotation in public dermoscopic image repositories
papers.summary: Dermoscopy is a widely adopted, non-invasive imaging technique that plays a crucial role in the early detection and clinical assessment of skin lesions (1). Its effectiveness, however, depends on the quality of the acquired images. In clinical practice, dermoscopic images often contain visual artifacts, such as hair, ruler markings, dark corners, bubbles, or ink traces, which are not part of the lesion itself. These artifacts can affect the visual appearance of the lesion, modifying color and texture patterns and complicating both clinical assessment and automated image analysis (2; 3; 4; 5).

papers.title: INTEGRATING ELEMENTARY MATHEMATICAL CONCEPTS AND SENSORY ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION IN PRE-SCHOOL CLIL SETTINGS
papers.summary: This expanded thesis investigates the dual methodological integration oflogical-mathematical structures and sensory-environmental exploration within earlychildhood English education using the Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL)framework. Based on systematic experiments at State Pre-school Educational OrganizationNo. 29, the study demonstrates how combining physical, hands-on micro-experiments andmathematical manipulations with the target language actively reinforces cognitive flexibilityand long-term vocabulary retention in young learners.

papers.title: Ancient oceans: Lapetus Ocean and Mirovia Ocean
papers.summary: Mirovia is conjectured to be an ancient superocean that surrounded the supercontinent Rodinia in Neoproterozoic Era 1,000 million to 541 million years ago. Like Iapetus Ocean [2020] , the work is intended as a companion to my realtime generative "Tectonic" works Rodinia, Vaalbara. It uses the notation developed for Tectonic: Rodinia [2016] and Pannotia, but does not involve any realtime manipulation of musical materials.

papers.title: WRCC2023_MI_A: WRCC2023 MI-A three-class motor imagery dataset
papers.summary: A three-class motor imagery EEG dataset (left hand, right hand, feet) from the MI-A track of the 2023 World Robot Contest BCI competition. It includes recordings from nine participants, two of whom are stroke patients, with 90 cued 4-second imagery trials each (30 per class). Data were acquired at 1000 Hz from 59 EEG channels using a Neuracle wireless system and re-released in BIDS format with HED annotations via MOABB.
